Let $L$ be a finite abelian extension of exponent dividing $m$. By
\cref{kummer:prob:kseq}\ref{kummer:it:kseq-res} and \cref{kummer:prop:inf-res}, with $\mu_m(\ksep)^{\Gal_L} = \mu_m(L) = \mu_m(\ksep)$,
\[
\Delta_L/k^{\times m} \cong \ker\bigl(H^1(k, \mu_m) \to H^1(L, \mu_m)\bigr)
\cong H^1(\Gal(L/k), \mu_m(L)) = \Hom(\Gal(L/k), \mu_m(L)),
\]
which has order $[L : k]$ by \cref{kummer:prop:characters}. Every element of $\Delta_L$ is an
$m$-th power in $L$, and then all its $m$-th roots lie in $L$, as $\mu_m(\ksep) \subseteq k$. So
$L' \coloneqq k(\Delta_L^{1/m}) \subseteq L$, and $[L' : k] = (\Delta_L : k^{\times m}) = [L : k]$
by \ref{kummer:it:kth-pairing}. Hence $L' = L$. Conversely, let $L = k(\Delta^{1/m})$. Then
$\Delta \subseteq \Delta_L$, and both have index $[L : k]$ over $k^{\times m}$, by
\ref{kummer:it:kth-pairing} and the computation above. So $\Delta = \Delta_L$.
\begin{solremark}
For $k = \Q$ and $m = 2$: the finite abelian extensions of $\Q$ of exponent $2$ are the
$\Q(\sqrt{d_1}, \dots, \sqrt{d_r})$, indexed by the finite subgroups of
$\Q^\times/\Q^{\times 2}$ \cite{Milne22}*{Example~5.31}.
\end{solremark}
\end{solution}
  \item\label{kummer:it:kth-cube} ($\star$) Let $k = \Q$, $m = 3$, $\zeta \in \Qbar$ a primitive
        cube root of unity, and $F \coloneqq \Q(\zeta)$. Here $\mu_3(\Qbar) \not\subseteq \Q$.
        \begin{enumerate}
          \item\label{kummer:it:kth-cube-fails} Show that $\Q(\sqrt[3]2)/\Q$ is not Galois,
                although $2 \notin \Q^{\times 3}$. Which step of \ref{kummer:it:kth-cyclic} fails?
\begin{solution}
\ans{\Cref{kummer:prop:trivial} fails: $\Gal_\Q$ acts nontrivially on $\mu_3(\Qbar)$.}
The real field $\Q(\sqrt[3]2)$ does not contain the other roots $\zeta\sqrt[3]2$,
$\zeta^2\sqrt[3]2$ of the irreducible polynomial $x^3 - 2$, so it is not normal. In
\ref{kummer:it:kth-cyclic}, \cref{kummer:prop:trivial} no longer applies: complex conjugation inverts
$\zeta$. The set $\{g : g(\alpha) = \alpha\} = \Gal_{\Q(\alpha)}$, for $\alpha = \sqrt[3]2$, is
still the set where the cocycle $\xi_g = g(\alpha)/\alpha$ is $1$, and it is still a
subgroup, but no longer the kernel of a homomorphism, and it is not normal.
\end{solution}
          \item\label{kummer:it:kth-cube-inj} Show that $\Q^\times/\Q^{\times 3} \to
                F^\times/F^{\times 3}$ is injective.\hint{\cref{kummer:prop:inf-res} and
                \cref{kummer:prob:cocycles}\ref{kummer:it:coc-order}.}
\begin{solution}
By \cref{kummer:prob:kseq}\ref{kummer:it:kseq-res} and \cref{kummer:prop:inf-res}, the kernel is isomorphic to
\[
H^1(\Gal(F/\Q), \mu_3(F)).
\]
This group is killed by $\#\Gal(F/\Q) = 2$
(\cref{kummer:prob:cocycles}\ref{kummer:it:coc-order}), and by $3$, since the cocycles take values in
$\mu_3(F)$. So it is trivial.
\begin{solremark}
An elementary proof: if $a = \beta^3$ with $\beta \in F$, then $a^2 = N_{F/\Q}(a) =
N_{F/\Q}(\beta)^3$, so $a = a^3/a^2 = (a/N_{F/\Q}(\beta))^3 \in \Q^{\times 3}$.
\end{solremark}
\end{solution}
          \item\label{kummer:it:kth-cube-s3} Let $a \in \Q^\times - \Q^{\times 3}$, $\alpha^3 = a$,
                and $L \coloneqq F(\alpha)$. Show that $L/\Q$ is Galois of degree $6$, and
                that conjugation by any $\tau \in \Gal(L/\Q)$ with $\tau(\zeta) = \zeta^{-1}$
                acts on $\Gal(L/F) \cong \mu_3(F)$, the isomorphism of
                \ref{kummer:it:kth-cyclic} over $F$, as inversion. Deduce that
                $\Gal(L/\Q) \cong S_3$. Check with \Magma:
\begin{magma}
R<x> := PolynomialRing(Rationals());
G := GaloisGroup(x^3 - 2);
#G, IsAbelian(G);                   // 6 false
F<zeta> := CyclotomicField(3);
S<y> := PolynomialRing(F);
#GaloisGroup(y^3 - 2);              // 3
\end{magma}
\begin{solution}
The field $L$ is generated by the roots $\alpha, \zeta\alpha, \zeta^2\alpha$ of $x^3 - a$,
so it is its splitting field, Galois over $\Q$. By \ref{kummer:it:kth-cube-inj}, $a$ is not a cube
in $F$, so $[L : F] = 3$ by \ref{kummer:it:kth-cyclic} over $F$, and $[L : \Q] = 6$. Let
$g \in \Gal(L/F)$ and $\omega \coloneqq g(\alpha)/\alpha \in \mu_3(F)$. The element
$\beta \coloneqq \tau^{-1}\alpha$ is another cube root of $a$, so
$g(\beta)/\beta = \omega$ too, as $g$ fixes $\mu_3(F) \subseteq F$. Then
\[
(\tau g\tau^{-1})(\alpha) = \tau(g(\beta)) = \tau(\omega\beta) = \tau(\omega)\,\alpha
= \omega^{-1}\alpha.
\]
So $\tau g\tau^{-1}$ corresponds to $\omega^{-1}$. Hence $\Gal(L/\Q)$, of order $6$, is
nonabelian, so it is $S_3$. \Magma\ agrees for $a = 2$: the group has order $6$ over $\Q$,
is not abelian, and has order $3$ over $F$.
\begin{solremark}
So $\Gal(L/F) \cong \mu_3(F)$ is an isomorphism of $\Gal(F/\Q)$-modules, for the action by
conjugation on the left and the natural action on the right, and it is the nontrivial
action on $\mu_3(F)$ that makes $L/\Q$ nonabelian. In cohomological terms,
\ref{kummer:it:kth-cube-inj} says that $\Res\colon H^1(\Q, \mu_3) \to H^1(F, \mu_3)$ is injective,
and its image lies in the $\Gal(F/\Q)$-invariants (compare
\cite{Silverman09}*{Exercise~B.3}, for finite groups).
\end{solremark}
\end{solution}
        \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\end{problem}


\section{Computing \texorpdfstring{$k^\times/k^{\times m}$}{k^x/k^xm}}
\label{kummer:sec:compute}

This section computes $k^\times/k^{\times m} \cong H^1(k, \mu_m)$ for finite fields,
$\Qp$ and $\Q$, and then cuts out a finite subgroup by conditions at the primes, as in
\cite{Poonen02}*{\S\S 9--10}. The last item is \cite{Silverman09}*{proof of Proposition~VIII.1.6}, with a \Magma\ check.

\begin{wslemma}[{Hensel's lemma \cite{Silverman09}*{Lemma~IV.1.2}}]
\label{kummer:lem:hensel}
Let $F \in \Z_p[w]$ and $a \in \Z_p$ with $F(a) \in p^n\Z_p$ for some $n \geq 1$ and
$F'(a) \in \Z_p^\times$. Then $F$ has a root $b \in \Z_p$ with $b \equiv a \pmod{p^n}$.
\end{wslemma}

\begin{wsdefinition}[{Unramified classes \cite{Poonen02}*{\S\S 4 and 9}}]
\label{kummer:def:unramified}
Let $p$ be a prime. Embed $\Qbar$ in an algebraic closure $\Qbar_p$ of $\Qp$, so that
restriction is an injection $\Gal_{\Qp} \coloneqq \Gal(\Qbar_p/\Qp) \hookrightarrow \Gal_\Q$.
Let $\Qp^{\unr} \subseteq \Qbar_p$ be the maximal unramified extension of $\Qp$, the union of
its finite unramified extensions. A finite extension of $\Qp$ inside $\Qbar_p$ is
unramified if and only if it lies in $\Qp^{\unr}$. The \defi{inertia group} is
$I_p \coloneqq \Gal(\Qbar_p/\Qp^{\unr}) \subseteq \Gal_{\Qp}$. A class
$\xi \in H^1(\Q, A)$, for a commutative algebraic group $A$ over $\Q$, is \defi{unramified
at $p$} if its image in $H^1(I_p, A(\Qbar_p))$ is trivial. For a
finite set $S$ of primes, $H^1(\Q, A; S)$ is the subgroup of the classes unramified at
every prime $p \notin S$.
\end{wsdefinition}

\begin{wsproposition}[{Unramified Kummer extensions \cite{Silverman09}*{proof of Proposition~VIII.1.6}}]
\label{kummer:prop:kummer-unramified}
Let $p$ be a prime with $p \nmid m$, $a \in \Qp^\times$ and $\alpha \in \Qbar_p$ with
$\alpha^m = a$. Then $\Qp(\alpha)/\Qp$ is unramified if and only if $v_p(a) \equiv 0
\pmod m$.
\end{wsproposition}

\begin{problem}[Finite and local fields]
\label{kummer:prob:local}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}
  \item\label{kummer:it:loc-finite} Let $q$ be a power of a prime not dividing $m$. Show that
        $\F_q^\times/\F_q^{\times m}$ is cyclic of order $\gcd(m, q - 1)$. If
        $m \mid q - 1$, so that $\mu_m(\Fbar_q) \subseteq \F_q$, compare the subgroups of
        $\F_q^\times/\F_q^{\times m}$ with the extensions of $\F_q$ of degree dividing $m$,
        as \cref{kummer:prob:kth}\ref{kummer:it:kth-bijection} predicts.
\begin{solution}
\ans{Both are indexed by the divisors of $m$.}
By \cref{kummer:prop:cyclic}, $\F_q^\times$ is cyclic of order $q - 1$. In a cyclic group $C$ of
order $n$, written additively as $\Z/n\Z$, the subgroup $mC$ is generated by $m$, of order
$n/\gcd(m, n)$, so $C/mC$ is cyclic of order $\gcd(m, n)$. If $m \mid q - 1$, the group
$\F_q^\times/\F_q^{\times m}$ is cyclic of order $m$, and its subgroups are indexed by the
divisors $d$ of $m$, with the subgroup of order $d$. On the other side, $\F_q$ has exactly
one extension of each degree $d$ inside an algebraic closure, $\F_{q^d}$, cyclic over
$\F_q$, and it has exponent dividing $m$ exactly when $d \mid m$. The bijection of
\cref{kummer:prob:kth}\ref{kummer:it:kth-bijection} matches the subgroup of order $d$ with $\F_{q^d}$.
\end{solution}
  \item\label{kummer:it:loc-odd} Let $p$ be odd and $u \in \Z_p^\times$ a unit whose reduction is
        not a square in $\F_p$. Show that $\Qp^\times/\Qp^{\times 2}$ has order $4$, with
        representatives $1, u, p, up$. List the quadratic extensions of $\Qp$, and say
        which one is unramified.\hint{every element of $\Qp^\times$ is $p^nv$ with $n \in
        \Z$ and $v \in \Z_p^\times$, and \cref{kummer:lem:hensel} decides which units are
        squares.}
\begin{solution}
\ans{$\Qp(\sqrt u)$, $\Qp(\sqrt p)$, $\Qp(\sqrt{up})$. Only $\Qp(\sqrt u)$ is unramified.}
If $v \in \Z_p^\times$ reduces to a square $\bar c^2$ in $\F_p$, with $c \in \Z_p^\times$,
then $F(w) \coloneqq w^2 - v$ has $F(c) \in p\Z_p$ and $F'(c) = 2c \in \Z_p^\times$, so $v$ is
a square by \cref{kummer:lem:hensel}. Conversely, squares of units reduce to squares. So
$\Z_p^\times/\Z_p^{\times 2} \cong \F_p^\times/\F_p^{\times 2}$, of order $2$ by
\ref{kummer:it:loc-finite}, with representatives $1, u$. As $\Qp^\times = p^{\Z} \times
\Z_p^\times$ and $p^2$ is a square, $\Qp^\times/\Qp^{\times 2}$ has order $4$, with
representatives $1, u, p, up$. By \cref{kummer:prob:kseq}\ref{kummer:it:kseq-quadratic}, the quadratic
extensions are $\Qp(\sqrt d)$ for $d = u, p, up$. By \cref{kummer:prop:kummer-unramified}, the
unramified one is $\Qp(\sqrt u)$, as $v_p(u) = 0$ is even.
\end{solution}
  \item\label{kummer:it:loc-two} Show that a unit $v \in \Z_2^\times$ is a square if and only if
        $v \equiv 1 \pmod 8$. Deduce that $\Q_2^\times/\Q_2^{\times 2}$ has order $8$, with
        representatives $\pm 1, \pm 2, \pm 5, \pm 10$. \Magma\ counts the quadratic
        extensions of $\Q_p$:
\begin{magma}
#AllExtensions(pAdicRing(3, 20), 2);    // 3
#AllExtensions(pAdicRing(5, 20), 2);    // 3
#AllExtensions(pAdicRing(2, 20), 2);    // 7
\end{magma}
        Check these against your answers.\hint{for $v \equiv 1 \pmod 8$, apply
        \cref{kummer:lem:hensel} to $F(w) = w^2 + w - (v - 1)/4$, then look at $(2w + 1)^2$.}
\begin{solution}
\ans{They agree: $3$ for odd $p$, and $8 - 1 = 7$ for $p = 2$.}
An odd integer has square $\equiv 1 \pmod 8$, and the same holds in $\Z_2$, by continuity,
so squares of units are $\equiv 1 \pmod 8$. Conversely, let $v \equiv 1 \pmod 8$ and
$c \coloneqq (v - 1)/4 \in 2\Z_2$. Then $F(w) = w^2 + w - c$ has $F(0) = -c \in 2\Z_2$ and
$F'(0) = 1$, so it has a root $b \in \Z_2$ by \cref{kummer:lem:hensel}, and
$(2b + 1)^2 = 4(b^2 + b) + 1 = 4c + 1 = v$. Hence
$\Z_2^\times/\Z_2^{\times 2} \cong (\Z/8\Z)^\times = \{\pm 1, \pm 5\}$, and
$\Q_2^\times/\Q_2^{\times 2}$, with $\Q_2^\times = 2^{\Z} \times \Z_2^\times$, has the eight
representatives $\pm 1, \pm 5, \pm 2, \pm 10$. By
\cref{kummer:prob:kseq}\ref{kummer:it:kseq-quadratic}, the quadratic extensions of $\Qp$ correspond to
the nontrivial classes: $3$ for odd $p$, by \ref{kummer:it:loc-odd}, and $7$ for $p = 2$.
\begin{solremark}
\Cref{kummer:prop:kummer-unramified} does not apply to $p = 2$ and $m = 2$. Of the seven quadratic
extensions of $\Q_2$, only $\Q_2(\sqrt 5) = \Q_2(\sqrt{-3})$ is unramified.
\end{solremark}
\end{solution}
\end{enumerate}
\end{problem}

\begin{wsdefinition}[{The group $k(S, m)$ \cite{Silverman09}*{Theorem~X.1.1(c)}}]
\label{kummer:def:kSm}
Let $k$ be a number field, $S$ a finite set of places of $k$ containing the archimedean
ones, and
\[
k(S, m) \coloneqq \{a \in k^\times/k^{\times m} : v(a) \equiv 0 \pmod m \text{ for all }
v \notin S\},
\]
where $v$ runs over the normalized valuations of $k$. Let $\calO_S$ be the ring of $S$-integers, the
$a \in k$ with $v(a) \geq 0$ for all $v \notin S$, and $\Cl(\calO_S)$ its ideal class
group. For $k = \Q$ we list only the primes in $S$, and in \cite{Poonen02}*{\S 10},
$\Q(S, 2)$ is written $\langle -1, S \rangle$.
\end{wsdefinition}

\begin{wsproposition}[{Finiteness \cite{Silverman09}*{proof of Proposition~VIII.1.6}}]
\label{kummer:prop:finiteness}
The group $\Cl(\calO_S)$ is finite, and $\calO_S^\times$ is finitely generated
(Dirichlet's $S$-unit theorem).
\end{wsproposition}

\begin{problem}[Classes unramified outside $S$]
\label{kummer:prob:global}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}
  \item\label{kummer:it:glob-basis} Show that $\Q^\times/\Q^{\times 2}$ is an $\F_2$-vector space
        with basis the classes of $-1$ and of the primes. In particular, it is infinite.
\begin{solution}
Every $a \in \Q^\times$ is $\pm\prod_p p^{v_p(a)}$, uniquely. Modulo squares only the sign
and the parities of the $v_p(a)$ matter, so
$a \mapsto (\operatorname{sign} a, (v_p(a) \bmod 2)_p)$ is an isomorphism from
$\Q^\times/\Q^{\times 2}$ to $\{\pm 1\} \times \bigoplus_p \Z/2\Z$, where the sum is over
the primes.
\end{solution}
  \item\label{kummer:it:glob-S} Let $S$ be a finite set of primes. Show that $\Q(S, 2)$ is the
        subgroup generated by $-1$ and the primes in $S$, of order $2^{\#S + 1}$.
\begin{solution}
In the coordinates of \ref{kummer:it:glob-basis}, $\Q(S, 2)$ is the set of classes whose
coordinates at the primes outside $S$ vanish, which is the span of $-1$ and the primes in
$S$.
\end{solution}
  \item\label{kummer:it:glob-unram} Let $p$ be an odd prime and $a \in \Q^\times$. Show that
        $\delta(a) \in H^1(\Q, \mu_2)$ is unramified at $p$ if and only if $v_p(a)$ is
        even. Deduce that $\Q(S, 2) = \delta^{-1}H^1(\Q, \mu_2; S)$ for every finite set
        $S$ of primes containing $2$.
\begin{solution}
The action of $I_p$ on $\mu_2(\Qbar_p) = \{\pm 1\}$ is trivial, so $H^1(I_p, \mu_2(\Qbar_p)) = \Hom_{\mathrm{conts}}(I_p,
\{\pm 1\})$ (\cref{kummer:prop:trivial}), and the restriction of $\delta(a)$ is the homomorphism
$g \mapsto g(\sqrt a)/\sqrt a$. It is trivial if and only if $I_p = \Gal(\Qbar_p/\Qp^{\unr})$
fixes $\sqrt a$, that is, if and only if $\sqrt a \in \Qp^{\unr}$ (\cref{kummer:prop:galois} over
$\Qp$), that is, by \cref{kummer:def:unramified}, if and only if $\Qp(\sqrt a)/\Qp$ is
unramified. By \cref{kummer:prop:kummer-unramified}, with $p \nmid 2$, this happens exactly
when $v_p(a)$ is even. So for $S \ni 2$, $\delta(a)$ is unramified at every $p \notin S$
exactly when $v_p(a)$ is even for every $p \notin S$, that is, when $a \in \Q(S, 2)$.
\begin{solremark}
This is the computation behind 2-descent: \cite{Poonen02}*{\S 10} identifies
$H^1(\Q, E[2]; S)$ with $\langle -1, S \rangle^2$ when $E[2](\Qbar) \subseteq E(\Q)$.
\end{solremark}
\end{solution}
  \item\label{kummer:it:glob-number} ($\star$) Let $k$ be a number field and $S$ as in
        \cref{kummer:def:kSm}. Construct an exact
        sequence\hint{the prime ideals of $\calO_S$ are those of the places outside $S$.
        If $a$ represents an element of $k(S, m)$, then $a\calO_S = \mathfrak a^m$ for a
        fractional ideal $\mathfrak a$ of $\calO_S$.}
        \[
        1 \to \calO_S^\times/\calO_S^{\times m} \to k(S, m) \to \Cl(\calO_S)[m] \to 0,
        \]
        and deduce that $k(S, m)$ is finite. For $k = \Q(\sqrt{-5})$, $m = 2$ and $S$ the
        archimedean place, show that $k(S, 2) = \langle -1, 2 \rangle$, of order $4$, and
        check with \Magma:
\begin{magma}
K<s> := QuadraticField(-5);
OK := Integers(K);
#ClassGroup(OK);                    // 2
G, m := pSelmerGroup(2, {PowerIdeal(OK)|});
#G;                                 // 4
[K | G.i @@ m : i in [1..Ngens(G)]];  // [ -1, 2 ]
\end{magma}
\begin{solution}
\ans{$a \mapsto [\mathfrak a]$, where $a\calO_S = \mathfrak a^m$.}
If $a$ represents an element of $k(S, m)$, its fractional ideal $a\calO_S$ has all
exponents divisible by $m$, so it is $\mathfrak a^m$ for a unique fractional ideal
$\mathfrak a$. Replacing $a$ by $ac^m$ replaces $\mathfrak a$ by $c\mathfrak a$, so
$a \mapsto [\mathfrak a]$ is a well defined homomorphism to $\Cl(\calO_S)$, with values in
$\Cl(\calO_S)[m]$, as $\mathfrak a^m$ is principal. It is surjective: if $\mathfrak a^m = a\calO_S$,
then $a$ represents an element of $k(S, m)$ mapping to $[\mathfrak a]$. Its kernel: if
$\mathfrak a = c\calO_S$, then $a/c^m \in \calO_S^\times$, so the kernel is the image of
$\calO_S^\times$. Finally, $u \in \calO_S^\times$ maps to $1$ in $k^\times/k^{\times m}$ if
$u = c^m$ with $c \in k^\times$, and then $c \in \calO_S^\times$, since $mv(c) = v(u) = 0$ for
$v \notin S$. So $\calO_S^\times/\calO_S^{\times m}$ injects. Both ends are finite by
\cref{kummer:prop:finiteness}, so $k(S, m)$ is finite.

For $k = \Q(\sqrt{-5})$ and $S$ archimedean, $\calO_S = \Z[\sqrt{-5}]$, with unit group
$\{\pm 1\}$, so $\calO_S^\times/\calO_S^{\times 2}$ is generated by $-1$. The class group has
order $2$ (\Magma), generated by $\mathfrak p \coloneqq (2, 1 + \sqrt{-5})$, which is not
principal, as no element of $\Z[\sqrt{-5}]$ has norm $2$. And
$\mathfrak p^2 = (2)$. So $2$ represents an element of $k(S, 2)$ mapping to $[\mathfrak p]$, and
$k(S, 2) = \langle -1, 2 \rangle$, of order $4$, as \Magma\ says.
\begin{solremark}
In the notation of \cref{kummer:def:unramified}, extended to $k$, $k(S, m) = H^1(k, \mu_m; S)$ when $S$ contains the places above $m$,
and the sequence is the Kummer sequence for the étale cohomology of $\operatorname{Spec}
\calO_S$, with $\Cl(\calO_S) = \Pic \calO_S$ in place of $H^1(k, \Gm) = 1$. Compare the
analogy between $\Cl(k)$ and the Shafarevich--Tate group in \cite{Poonen02}*{\S 7}.
\end{solremark}
\end{solution}
\end{enumerate}
\end{problem}

\begin{bibdiv}
\begin{biblist}

\bib{Magma}{article}{
      author={Bosma, Wieb},
      author={Cannon, John},
      author={Playoust, Catherine},
       title={The {M}agma algebra system. {I}. {T}he user language},
        date={1997},
        ISSN={0747-7171},
     journal={J. Symbolic Comput.},
